Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the run-through this morning. We're attaching a redline of your standard MSA + a proposed Order Form spreadsheet; the two items below are the primary asks from our legal/compliance teams: 

1) Output title: Helix needs assignment of "Output Title" for any outputs that are incorporated into our diagnostic product modules (Exhibit A lists these endpoints). We understand this is an unusual ask — we're trying to avoid downstream IP disputes with OEM partners.

2) Training & telemetry: Our data is highly sensitive (PHI-adjacent). We need an explicit exclusion so Helix-provided prompts/data are not used to improve or train the general model and must be segregated from telemetry used for service analytics.

We are open to scoped language and a limited-term carveout, but we need clear contractual language. Please review the attached redline and let us know if Redwood can accept a narrow assignment for the named endpoints or propose an equivalent license structure.

We typically do not assign title to generated outputs, but we can discuss a scoped exception for explicitly listed endpoints where Helix will integrate content into a product shipped to end users.

Proposed next steps from our side: 
- Internal legal (laura.bennett) to propose precise carveout language that converts "assignment" to a "limited assignment for specific endpoints" or an "exclusive perpetual license" for the listed Deliverables.
- Engineering/infra to put a technical segregation plan on paper (segregated telemetry bucket + no-training flag). Aditya, can you confirm the feasibility and whether we should add a service-level labeling requirement to the Order Form?
- Quick sync (30 min) with Helix legal + procurement to align on timing — is Thursday at 10am PT doable?

If we can agree on narrow scope and evidence controls (audit logs, encrypted telemetry, retention windows) I think we can close this without changing Redwood's broader IP playbook. Sending to legal for language.

Marissa / Aditya — I reviewed Helix's redline and drafted suggested language that (a) avoids full assignment, but (b) grants Helix an exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable license to Outputs generated by the model when used solely in the Helix Product Endpoints enumerated in Exhibit A of the Order Form. Key points: 

- Scope: limited to the endpoints and Deliverables defined in Attachment A; all other outputs remain governed by Redwood's standard license.
- Training: add explicit clause: "Customer Data and Customer-Provided Prompts shall not be used to train or improve Redwood's public or shared models. Redwood shall process such data only within a segregated environment and may retain telemetry solely for debugging and billing, subject to the retention window in Section X."
- Audit & evidence: require quarterly audit statements and on-demand audit rights for a limited number of requests per year.

I attach the draft redline (Helix_MSA_redline_v1_redlined_by_redwood.docx). If Sales is comfortable, I recommend we present the license approach rather than assignment — it meets Helix's downstream protection goals while keeping Redwood's IP standard.

Marissa — I also flagged two minor commercial asks that will need exec approval: (1) 12-month transition pricing for the exclusivity on the listed endpoints; (2) liability cap carveouts tied to PHI-adjacent exposures. Please advise whether pricing can be proposed to Helix procurement.
